scope.policy: source-first shortlist against active canonical registry, not an exhaustive European census

governance: A new candidate is not an approved shrine, a mapped Place or a user-facing object until reconciled separately against the canonical owner.
One physical site can have many separately sourced pilgrimage, relic and reported-apparition associations, but should have one canonical Place identity.
The Italian sanctuary association, the RME network, and bishops' curated selections are source discovery lists, not complete national registries.
A juridical sanctuary claim requires ecclesiastical status, especially in Spain: do not call Torreciudad a canonically recognized sanctuary on the strength of popular usage.
French-world domestic custom relevance gate remains in force; other regional events may be registered as contextual heritage only with explicit source and scope.
Coordinates, route geometry, opening hours, biographies and artwork are deliberately deferred.
Site institutional recognition and supernatural authenticity of apparitions must be independently checked, following DDF 2024 Norms.
Cross-confessional Catholic/Orthodox/Lutheran heritage must preserve the actual current custodial tradition; a shared sacred image does not by itself create a Latin Catholic cult claim.
